shadows.name: eyebrow

components.name: Primary CTA
components.description: The confident action — Book on OpenTable, "Pick one for us." Marine (tint) fill, card text, full pill, soft neutral eyebrow. Hover brightens the fill; never shifts layout.

components.name: Price Pill
components.description: The one saturated object per screen — the flamingo price pill, price only. Rounded --r-sm, card text.

components.name: Facet Pill
components.description: A filter option with a live mono count. --sunk fill, full pill, ink label, >=44px. Hover washes to --marine-wash with tint text; selected = marine (tint) fill + card text. Zero-count options are disabled and greyed, never removed.

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: iOS pattern — a --sunk track (--r-md, 3px inset) with a soft neutral --card thumb (--r-sm, eyebrow) on the selected segment. List/Map view and the course strip. Neutral thumb for exclusive choices; tint fill is reserved for multi-select.

components.name: Applied Filter Chip
components.description: A removable applied filter. Marine (tint) fill, card text, an x, full pill; every discovery/mood/occasion selection resolves to one so nothing is a hidden query.

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Apple's filled search field — --sunk fill, transparent border, --r-md, >=44px. On focus the background lifts to --card and the border shifts to --marine. No glow.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Search a name, cuisine, dish…" />

components.name: Result Row
components.description: The signature unit — three tiers (name / cuisine-hood-dishes meta / course-aware teaser), a bookmark pin in a fixed left gutter, the flamingo price pill and availability on the right, a single --hair bottom border. The whole row is the disclosure control and washes to --marine-wash on hover.

narrative.overview: The colour soul is Miami Vice after dark; the form is a native Apple app. Apple HIG form — SF system faces, continuous rounded corners, soft neutral depth, generous rhythm, sentence case, iOS-grade controls, rows-not-cards — carries a Miami Vice night soul: a deep-marine after-hours field, the Vice cyan as the single interactive tint, and one hot-pink flamingo reserved for price. The two Vice hues surface only as the system tint and one saturated object, never as the wall itself. This is "Miami Vice" reached by exclusion, per Michael Mann's production rule — no earth tones, no primaries, no glow — deliberately the opposite of the neon-on-black synthwave that reads as machine-made. The 2026-08-02 redesign retired the Tropical Deco pass (hard offset slabs, square corners, racing stripes, a Poiret-One uppercase wordmark over Jost), kept as historical anti-reference in DESIGN_REVIEW.md / VICE_DIRECTION.md. The product ships night-only (:root[data-theme='pm'], forced in main.js); :root holds a dormant light fallback.
keyCharacteristics: Deep-marine night field; colour lives only in the cyan system tint and the one flamingo price.
Depth is soft and neutral — a low-blur rgba(0,0,0,…) offset, never a hard slab, never a colored glow.
Continuous rounded corners — three radius steps plus a pill — Apple's soft geometry.
SF system type, sentence case, a fuller Apple text ramp; no web fonts, no uppercase eyebrows.
iOS controls: filled tracks with a soft neutral thumb; tint-filled selection; >=44pt targets.
Rows, not cards — a 380-item comparison directory, ~8.7 per 900px viewport.

rules.name: The Price-Only Rule
rules.body: --flamingo is used for price and nothing else. Its scarcity makes it the memory anchor; spend it anywhere else and the isolation collapses.

rules.name: The Tint Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the single interactive tint — selection, links, filled controls, the primary CTA — exactly as an Apple app uses one accent. It never becomes the field and is never blurred into a glow.

rules.name: The Night Rule
rules.body: The app is night-only — the deep-marine set ships. Every small-text pair clears Apple's 7:1 on both field and card; the lighter :root tokens remain a dormant, AA-clean fallback with no daytime mode in the product.

rules.name: The Apple-Ramp Rule
rules.body: Six weight-and-size steps — 13 / 15 / 17 / 22 / 28 / display(32–44) — with fewer than three adjacent pairs under 1.15×. Hierarchy is made by weight and tracking as much as size.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text-transform is retired entirely. Labels lead in sentence case; a re-introduced uppercase role risks the eyebrow-overuse tell. The content, not the label, carries emphasis.

rules.name: The Soft-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a soft neutral rgba(0,0,0,…) offset, never a hard slab and never a halo. A coloured blur is the banned slop tell; reach for tonal surface steps and hairlines first.

rules.name: The Continuous-Round Rule
rules.body: Everything is rounded; keep at least three distinct radii (--r-sm/md/lg + --r-full) in play or the uniform-radius tell fires. If a control needs to read tighter, change its radius step, not its corners to zero.

rules.name: The Rows-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: A 380-item comparison directory hits all four NN/g cases where cards are wrong (search, comparison, homogeneous content, density). Results stay rows (~104px, >=5 per 900px viewport); secondary actions move into the expanded panel.

dos: Do route every colour through a var(); raw hex outside app.css is a lint finding.
Do express depth with the soft neutral --eyebrow / --shadow-lg and tonal surface steps.
Do round continuously — keep >=3 distinct radii (--r-sm/md/lg + --r-full) in play.
Do keep results as rows at ~104px, >=5 per 900px viewport; move secondary actions into the expanded panel.
Do reserve --flamingo for price and let the single cyan tint carry all other interaction.
Do keep type sentence case on the Apple ramp (13 / 15 / 17 / 22 / 28 / display).
Do disable-and-grey zero-count options; never remove them.
Do keep every control's hit target >=44pt and meet the floors: 11px min type, 7:1 small text, 3:1 UI boundary.
donts: Don't use a coloured glow, gradient text, glassmorphism, or a radial aurora background — every one is a catalogued AI-slop tell and a design-lint.mjs failure. Neutral rgba(0,0,0) shadows are fine.
Don't put neon on the field: the Vice hues are the tint and one price object, never the wall.
Don't re-introduce uppercase eyebrows, a hard zero-blur offset slab, square corners, or the retired Deco devices (horizon bar, racing stripes, Poiret wordmark).
Don't use --flamingo for anything but price, or a second isolated accent that dilutes it.
Don't reach for a card grid, a web font (Inter / Geist / Space Grotesk / Poppins), or pure #000/#fff.
Don't work around a lint rule — if you disagree with it, edit the rule and say why.

newestComponents.name: MenuSheet
newestComponents.body: The accessible full-menu meal-detail modal. Opened per meal from the CourseLadder ("See the full [meal] menu, with descriptions"), it shows every course, the choose-count, and each dish with its description note. A real modal: portalled to <body>, focus moved in and restored, Esc + backdrop close, background scroll locked, role=dialog + aria-modal. Bottom-sheet on mobile, centered >=640px, rising in on open. Its header is a deliberate Vice moment — the meal title over a --marine-wash band with the flamingo price sitting inside it.

newestComponents.name: ViceMark
newestComponents.body: The flat cyan Miami-sun brand mark: a banded sunset over a horizon line, authored SVG, solid currentColor fills only — no gradient, no glow (the banned synthwave tells). Coloured by the cyan tint, never the price flamingo, so the price-only rule stands. Used as the masthead brand mark, the image-fallback tile, and the results empty-state mark.
